extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners, patent examiners, and third-party requesters involved in inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for conducting and responding in inter partes reexamination proceedings, including timing, briefing, amendments, supplemental responses, extensions, service, and amendment formalities. Focuses on requirements for patent owners, third-party requesters, and examiners under relevant CFR provisions and MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended brief for non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who is notified of non-compliance of an appellant brief or respondent brief must file an amended brief within a non-extendable time period of one month from the date of the Office letter notifying the party of the non-compliance of the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time is non-extendable; file within one month from mailing of Office letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal brief after examiner's answer
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party requester appellant and/or a patent owner appellant may each file a rebuttal brief within one month of the date of the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for filing a rebuttal brief may not be extended. See 37 CFR 41.66(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request timing and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If an appellant or a respondent (who has filed a respondent brief) desires an oral hearing by the Board, he or she must file a written request for an oral hearing accompanied by the fee within two months after the date of the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for filing a request for oral hearing may not be extended. See 37 CFR 41.73(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Court timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for the patent owner and/or the third party requester to file a notice of appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit is two months from the date of the Board decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a timely request for rehearing (37 CFR 41.79) is filed, the time is two months from final Board action on the request for rehearing. See 37 CFR 1.304(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time in an inter partes reexamination proceeding are governed by 37 CFR 1.956; extensions of time are otherwise governed by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Director or SPRS where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2665 and 37 CFR 1.956. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a)/(b) do NOT apply to inter partes reexamination. Extensions of time are not available to third party requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing of Office action and correspondence address
rubrics_metrics.description: After an Office action is completed and approved by CRU SPRS or TC QAS, the action is mailed. Inter partes reexamination forms are structured to print identifying information and the correspondence address (official correspondence address of record in the patent file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no official correspondence address exists, the Office may treat the mailing address as correspondence address. Where multiple patent owners exist, the Office may use the first-named patent owner’s mailing address; the Office will not engage in double correspondence. Copies of actions are mailed to third party requesters using transmittal form PTOL-2070.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension request filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an extension of time must be filed on or before the day on which action by the patent owner is due and must set forth sufficient cause and a reasonable time specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be accompanied by the petition set forth in § 1.17(g) and the petition fee. Mere filing of a request does not effect any extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of 'sufficient cause' for extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of whether 'sufficient cause' has been shown must balance providing the patent owner a fair opportunity to respond against the statutory requirement that proceedings be conducted with special dispatch (35 U.S.C. 314(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must fully state reasons including (A) what action the patent owner has taken to provide a response to date, and (B) why additional time is needed despite such action. The statement must provide a factual accounting of reasonably diligent behavior by those responsible for preparing a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical extension grant practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution will be conducted by initially setting a time period of at least 30 days or one month (whichever is longer). First requests for extensions are granted for sufficient cause and usually for one month; second or subsequent requests or requests for more than one month are granted only in extraordinary situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reasons; first requests favorably considered where factual accounting shows reasonable diligence. See MPEP § 2662.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions for affidavits after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for an extension of time to submit an affidavit after an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) may be granted, but the entry of the affidavit is subject to the examiner's scrutiny as to why it was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If showing is insufficient, the examiner may deny entry of the affidavit notwithstanding grant of the extension. Affidavits submitted after an ACP are treated like amendments submitted after an ACP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner reply substance requirement (37 CFR 1.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the patent owner must reply in writing, distinctly and specifically pointing out supposed errors in the examiner’s action and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references; a general allegation of patentability without specifics is inadequate. Show how amendments avoid references and why any 35 U.S.C. 112 rejections are incorrect or inapplicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies limited entry (37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental reply will not be entered as a matter of right except where it is clearly limited to: (A) cancellation of claim(s); (B) adoption of examiner suggestion(s); (C) placement of the proceeding in condition for allowance/NIRC; (D) reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply was filed; (E) correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors); or (F) simplification of issues for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental reply will be entered if filed within the period during which action by the Office is suspended under § 1.103(a) or (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response timing and service (37 CFR 1.945)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner will be given at least thirty days to interfile a response to any Office action on the merits in the inter partes reexamination and must serve a copy of the response on the third party requester in accordance with 37 CFR 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of service can prevent the third party requester from timely filing comments (must file within 30 days from date of service). Patent owner normally given two months to respond; extensions only via 37 CFR 1.956.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental response entry showing (37 CFR 1.945(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplemental response must be accompanied by a showing of sufficient cause why the supplemental response should be entered, including: (1) explanation of how 37 CFR 1.111(a)(2)(i) are satisfied; (2) explanation why not presented with the original response; and (3) a compelling reason to enter the supplemental response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the showing is not provided the supplemental response will not be entered and may be sealed (closed) from public view in the IFW.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if supplemental response not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplemental response is not entered, it and any comments following may be returned to the parties or discarded; if already scanned into IFW they may be marked 'closed' and 'non-public' and will not constitute part of the record or be displayed in PAIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner wishes unentered supplemental response considered later, include its contents in a proper response to a subsequent Office action; entry rules for responses to an ACP or closing prosecution governed by 37 CFR 1.116 and 1.951(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party paper handling with patent owner response
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner cannot file papers on behalf of a third party. If a third party paper accompanies or is submitted as part of a timely filed patent owner response, the entire submission is an improper (informal) submission and shall be returned to the patent owner; the third party paper will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return using form PTOL-2069; provide appropriate period for patent owner to refile response without the third party paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester comments timing to preserve rights (35 U.S.C. 314(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any requester comments filed after a patent owner response to an Office action must be filed 'within 30 days after the date of service of the patent owner’s response' to satisfy 35 U.S.C. 314(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where patent owner files a supplemental response, requesters should file comments within 30 days after service to preserve comment rights in case the Office enters the supplemental response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments by patent owner must comply with 1.530(d)-(j) and 1.943
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the description and claims in patents involved in reexamination proceedings must be made in accordance with § 1.530 and related rules, and amendments in inter partes reexamination are made by filing a paper in compliance with §§ 1.530(d)-(k) and 1.943.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must be formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a)-(b) and contain required fees per 37 CFR 1.20(c). Use Manner of Making Amendments guidance in MPEP §2250 and MPEP §2234 for entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment paper must include the entire text of each patent claim proposed to be changed and each new claim proposed to be added; for changed claims include a parenthetical 'amended', 'twice amended', etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changed and added claims must include markings per paragraph (f) (matter to be omitted in brackets, matter to be added underlined); a claim canceled may be canceled by statement without presenting text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and drawing amendment format
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to the specification other than claims must be made by submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph including markings and must identify precise insertion points. Drawings changes must be submitted as a sketch on separate paper showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon approval file new sheets of drawings complying with §1.84; amended figures identified as 'Amended', added figure as 'New', canceled figures bracketed and identified as 'Canceled.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and support for claim changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever there is an amendment to the claims, supply on pages separate from the changes the status (pending or canceled) of all patent claims and all added claims as of the date of the amendment, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure for the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear basis showing support in specification for amendments; required to permit evaluation of new/changed claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes shown by markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes made to the specification, including the claims, must show matter to be omitted enclosed in brackets and matter to be added underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markings apply whether amendment submitted on paper or compact disc. See paragraph (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered; numbering of any claims added must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to renumber existing claims when inserting new claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope; no new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter; no amendment (other than cancellation) will be incorporated into an expired patent by certificate after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended or new claims which broaden or enlarge a claim should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 314(a). Apply same test as reissue enlarging claims (see In re Freeman and MPEP §2658). See MPEP §2670 for new matter handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not effective until reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though entered, proposed amendments will not be effective until the reexamination certificate is issued and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should understand amendments affect prosecution but do not modify patent rights until certificate under 35 U.S.C. 316 is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent expiration on amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent expires during the reexamination procedure and the patent claims have been amended, the Office will hold the amendments as improper and subsequent reexamination will proceed on the basis of the unamended patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once patent expires, a narrow claim construction is applied. See MPEP §2258 subsection I.G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment entry criteria and forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and 1.943, are formally presented and contain required fees will be entered in the reexamination file pursuant to MPEP §2234 guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 22.12 may be used to advise patent owner of manner of making amendments; form paragraph 26.05.01 or PTOL-2069 box 4 may be used to notify of improper amendments. A shortened statutory period for correction may be set to ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When it appears the correct inventor(s) were not named through error without deceptive intention, the Director may, on petition of all parties with satisfactory proof and payment of fee, include in the reexamination certificate an amendment naming only the actual inventor(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must satisfy §1.324 and be submitted as part of the reexamination proceeding. If reexamination concludes other than by certificate, a certificate of correction can be issued upon request by the patentee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of mailing/transmission and filing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing and the certificate of transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) and the Priority Mail Express® mailing procedure (37 CFR 1.10) may be used to file requests for extension of time and other papers in an existing inter partes reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these procedures to establish timely filing dates where appropriate; see MPEP §2666 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of patent drawings (detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner; upon approval, new sheets complying with §1.84 must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify amended figures as 'Amended', any added figure as 'New', and canceled figures bracketed and identified as 'Canceled.' See MPEP §2666.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADS submission restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner cannot submit an application data sheet (ADS) in a reexamination proceeding except as provided in MPEP §2258.02.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not file ADS except under the limited circumstances specified in the cited MPEP subsection.
